name: Question 3
problem: Given that $u=x+1,$ which integral is equivalent to $\int \frac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{x+1}}\,\text{d}x?$
worked_solution:
Since $u=x+1,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

We also note that 
$x=u-1.$

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{x+1}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{(u-1)^{2}}{\sqrt{u}}\text{d}u \\  & =\int ({u}^{2}-2u+1){u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int ({u}^{3/2}-2{u}^{1/2}+{u}^{-1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\int (\sqrt{{u}^{3}}-2\sqrt{u}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}})\,\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Given that u=x+1, which integral is equivalent to ∫x2x+1dx?

a
∫(u3−2u2+1u)du
b
∫(u3−2u)du
c
∫(u3+1u)du
d
∫(1u−2u)du
e
∫(u3−2u+1u)du
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since u=x+1, we have dudx=1⟹du=dx.

We also note that x=u−1.

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of u:

∫x2x+1dx=∫(u−1)2udu=∫(u2−2u+1)u−1/2du=∫(u3/2−2u1/2+u−1/2)du=∫(u3−2u+1u)du
